subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: For Dashboard `/compact` on ordinary `claude-cli` sessions that are near or past the native context cap, should OpenClaw fail loudly, trust Claude Code native compaction, or implement OpenClaw-owned fallback recovery?
rationale: Current source intentionally treats Claude CLI compaction as backend-owned, while the reported failure involves Dashboard recovery, native transcript ownership, and session-state data loss semantics that require an explicit product/runtime contract before automation can safely implement a fix.

options.title: Fail Loudly Until Recovery Is Proven
options.body: Keep Claude CLI compaction backend-owned for now, but make Dashboard and session lifecycle recovery refuse with clear export/manual-prune guidance and never rotate or checkpoint empty context.

options.title: Accept Full Native Delegation
options.body: Continue relying on Claude Code compaction only after maintainers obtain live proof that native compaction preserves resumable context past the cap and can surface a trustworthy result to OpenClaw.

options.title: Build OpenClaw Fallback Recovery
options.body: Implement a tested OpenClaw-owned over-cap recovery path that reads bounded native Claude transcript content or uses a fallback model before any session rotation.

recommendation.title: Fail Loudly Until Recovery Is Proven
recommendation.body: Keep Claude CLI compaction backend-owned for now, but make Dashboard and session lifecycle recovery refuse with clear export/manual-prune guidance and never rotate or checkpoint empty context.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the native compaction ownership contract and are the best available routing owner for deciding whether that shipped deferral remains acceptable for Dashboard over-cap recovery.
